InsideOfTruck_EventScript_SetIntroFlags.reason: The gender branch of the truck's exit-tile trigger, ported as its flag/var effect: assets::new_game_flags::TRUCK_INTRO_FLAGS_MALE/_FEMALE (5 setflags each) and TRUCK_INTRO_VARS_MALE/_FEMALE (VAR_LITTLEROOT_INTRO_STATE, VAR_LITTLEROOT_HOUSES_STATE_BRENDAN/_MAY), applied by crate::new_game::apply_truck_intro_flags at new-game init. Upstream this is a coord (trigger) event on all three truck exit tiles gated on VAR_LITTLEROOT_INTRO_STATE == 0 (data/maps/InsideOfTruck/map.json:85-112), so it fires exactly once on the way out of the truck and every real playthrough passes through it before reaching a house; this port skips the truck sequence entirely, so new-game init is the point the skipped flow would have produced the effect -- same 'the effect, without an interpreter' shape as the EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags application beside it. Load-bearing rather than cosmetic now that object-event visibility gates collision and rendering (issue #161): without it a fresh save reaches the player's house with the rival's Poke Ball spawned in the bedroom as an invisible collider and the rival's mother and sibling spawned in the player's own 1F (a duplicated mother plus another undrawn blocker). The two branches are exact Brendan/May mirrors, and a playerGender byte outside MALE/FEMALE applies neither, matching the script's own missing else. As of issue #261, the leading setrespawn HEAL_LOCATION_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_{BRENDANS,MAYS}_HOUSE_2F line IS modelled too -- crate::new_game::default_last_heal_location reproduces its SetLastHealLocationWarp effect (gender-branched, same fallback-to-no-op for an out-of-range gender byte), applied to SaveBlock1::last_heal_location alongside this artifact's own flags/vars at init_save_blocks time; see src/overworld.c#SetLastHealLocationWarp for the full citation. Still not modelled: setdynamicwarp MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN (no dynamic-warp destination state), the lockall/releaseall pair, and setflag FLAG_HIDE_MAP_NAME_POPUP (outside both gender branches; no map-name popup is rendered). Required for correctness, not cosmetics: decoration placeholders invert the usual polarity (an EMPTY slot is the flag-SET state), nothing sets these at new-game time (InitEventData zeroes all flags; EventScript_ResetAllMapFlags never mentions them), and upstream relies purely on ordering -- RunOnTransitionMapScript (overworld.c:860) precedes TrySpawnObjectEvents (overworld.c:2163-2178) -- so without it a fresh save reads all twelve bedroom placeholders as spawned, i.e. as invisible blockers (DoesObjectCollideWithObjectAt consults only active, coordinates and elevation, never the invisible flag, so even MOVEMENT_TYPE_INVISIBLE would still block). Stubbed, not rewritten: no script interpreter runs this, and the maps that call it are a transcribed list rather than a parsed map-script table. Not modelled: the secret-base callers (data/scripts/shared_secret_base.inc:12-16) and flags 13/14's secret-base-only slots.

BattleAI_DoAIProcessing.reason: battle_ai_script_commands.c:572. The per-moveset-index driver loop modelled inside battle::trainer_ai::choose_trainer_action (issue #237): each enabled script runs once for every slot 0..MAX_MON_MOVES, and a slot whose moveConsidered reads as 0 -- an unfilled MOVE_NONE slot, or one with 0 PP (:582-:584) -- has its score zeroed and its script SKIPPED, so it costs no RNG draws at all. That skip is RNG-observable, which is why it is modelled rather than approximated by scoring every slot. The AIState_DoNotProcess/AIState_SettingUp/AIState_Processing state machine itself is not reproduced (it is control-flow structure, not behaviour -- oop-boundaries), nor is AI_ACTION_DO_NOT_ATTACK's early exit, which none of the four modelled scripts sets. affine_tile_layer.reason: AffineTilemap/AffineBgLayer port SetBgAffine/SetBgAffineInternal-driven mode 1/2 affine BG semantics: 8bpp-only flat single-byte tile indices (no per-tile flip/palette bank), P/Q matrix (AffineMatrix, affine.rs) + 20.8 fixed-point reference-point texture-space sampling, and wrap (overflow=1) vs transparent (overflow=0) out-of-bounds handling, verified against mgba's GBAVideoSoftwareRendererDrawBackgroundMode2 and MODE_2_COORD_OVERFLOW/NO_OVERFLOW macros (software-bg.c). AffineBgLayer::sample_column_with_mosaic_hold adds the stateful transparent-overflow mosaic path: an off-map column is retried on the next column instead of blanking the rest of its block, an accepted column holds for the whole block (a palette-index-0 texel included), decoded horizontal block sizes 1 and 2 hold nothing, and a span reopening mid-block seeds its hold from the snapped block origin -- gated on the column before the span, yet fetched with wrapping rather than bounds-tested. The per-scanline sx/sy accumulation mgba's renderer performs collapses into one static per-frame closed-form sample under pokeemerald's observed once-per-frame BG2X/Y/PA..PD write pattern (bg.c:244-282); a game that rewrote the reference point mid-frame would observe different behavior, out of scope here. Slots into compose_frame via BgSlot::new_affine (issue #98, issue #872).

mosaic.reason: BgSlot::with_mosaic (compositor.rs) plus crate::mosaic::MosaicSize/MosaicConfig port BGxCNT's mosaic bit and the shared MOSAIC register's BG H/V block-size fields, verified against mgba's BACKGROUND_BITMAP_INIT mosaic macros (S-2 slice 4, issue #99). Stateless top-left snapping (coord - coord % size at composite time) covers regular 4bpp BGs and affine layers with wrap overflow, which additionally bypass horizontal snapping at decoded block sizes 1 and 2 (BgSlot::wrap_affine_bypasses_horizontal_mosaic). An affine layer with transparent overflow is not stateless: it runs the per-column AffineMosaicHold in bg_affine.rs, which retries past a rejected origin instead of blanking the block, holds the accepted texel for the rest of the block, holds nothing at decoded sizes 1 and 2, and seeds a mid-block reopened span from the snapped origin behind the preceding-column gate; compose_frame resets that hold at every surviving window span start on the scanline (issue #872). A regular 8bpp BG with horizontal size above 1 is per-span, not stateless: a window span starting mid-block holds the span-start pixel column of the scrolled start (BgLayer::sample_8bpp_mosaic_prefetch, selecting the tile by mGBA's (16 + offset) >> 3 rule) until the next block boundary, restarting at every pass start, verified against mgba's DRAW_BACKGROUND_MODE_0_MOSAIC_256 (software-mode0.c:320-408; issue #2026). Complements regular_tile_layer/affine_tile_layer/scroll_wrapping.

regular_tile_layer.reason: BgLayer/ScreenEntry/Tilemap port the regular (non-affine) BG tile-layer compositing semantics: screen-entry tile index/flip/palette-bank bits, 4bpp/8bpp tile-to-pixel resolution, transparent palette index 0 (every bank), and >32-tile tilemaps addressed as 32x32 screenblocks, verified against mgba's software mode-0 renderer; scrolling, affine BGs, and multi-layer priority are out of scope for this slice (issue #50).

scroll_wrapping.reason: BgLayer::composite_scrolled/sample_scrolled port ChangeBgX/ChangeBgY's 9-bit wrapping regular-BG scroll offsets: the visible window wraps within the tilemap's own pixel size (256/512px per axis for a hardware-sized regular BG), verified against mgba's software mode-0 renderer; affine BG scroll/rotation is out of scope (issue #64).

DoesObjectCollideWithObjectAt.reason: COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT: the destination-tile occupancy test, re-implemented as PlayerState::step's third and last collision check (after the grid collision bits and the elevation mismatch, matching GetCollisionAtCoords' own test order), via engine::overworld::object_event::visible_object_event_at over the runtime's bound live ObjectEventCollection, so a moved object blocks its live tile and vacates its authored one. AreElevationsCompatible is the same either-side-ELEVATION_TRANSITION wildcard predicate MapRuntime::object_events_at applies. Narrowed: upstream's curObject != objectEvent self-skip has no counterpart (the player is a PlayerState, never a collection entry); upstream's second previousCoords term is not modelled, because ObjectEventState retains its previous position with no animation-completion lifecycle and reserving it would block the vacated tile indefinitely; a connection-crossing step does not run the test at all because ConnectedMapData exposes no neighbouring-map event data.

GetObjectEventIdByPosition.reason: Position-plus-elevation-wildcard object-event scan rewritten as MapRuntime::object_events_at. With a bound ObjectEventCollection (MapRuntime::with_object_events) it delegates to ObjectEventCollection::object_events_at and compares each object's live position and elevation, returning the authored template as metadata; a bound collection never falls back to authored coordinates. Unbound runtimes (trainer sight) still scan authored coordinates. ObjectEventDoesElevationMatch's rule (either side's ELEVATION_TRANSITION is a wildcard) is the shared collision::elevations_compatible predicate. It returns an iterator over every match on the tile, not a single hit, because upstream only scans spawned object events (a set hide flag prevents the spawn) while this port scans every template: the hide-flag filter therefore runs inside the scan, in engine::overworld::object_event::visible_object_event_at. Both consumers, the facing lookup (facing_object_event) and PlayerState::step's COLLISION_OBJECT_EVENT check, go through that one composed search. Templates stack per tile with independent flags (the Birch lab's three starter balls at (6, 8)). Known narrowing: live elevation is the retained state elevation, which no writer updates from the ground (ObjectEventUpdateElevation, event_object_movement.c:1758-1770, :8089); trainer sight and cross-map objects are not migrated.

Because the filter is applied at query time rather than at spawn time, every such search applies it *inside* its scan, so a tile carrying several stacked templates with independent hide flags resolves to the first visible one, exactly as scanning a spawned-only gObjectEvents would. Subpriority is modelled: npc::subpriority computes sElevationToSubpriority[elevation] (:7691-7693, npc::ELEVATION_TO_SUBPRIORITY) + (16 - (((y + 8) & 0xFF) >> 4)) * 2 + 1 from SetObjectSubpriorityByElevation (:7739-7745), with y the OBJ's rendered top plus its 32px height, and npc::order_by_depth sorts the whole OAM list by ascending OBJ priority, then subpriority, so the lower subpriority of each OBJ priority gets the lower OAM index (the renderer keeps the earlier entry on an equal-priority tie) and slot order matches what SortSprites hands the PPU across priorities (#1630), equal subpriorities falling to the lower on-screen y first as SortSprites does (sprite.c:413-415) and full ties keeping player-then-template order; the elevation base matters because elevations 2 and 3 share priority 2. gPlayerRunMovementActions.reason: The four-direction run action table collapses to TransitCadence::RUN at the crossing's chosen direction (event_object_movement.c:968-974).

CameraUpdate.reason: Per-frame gFieldCamera pixel-offset accumulator (movementSpeedX/Y ramping gTotalCameraPixelOffsetX/Y by 1px/frame toward a full metatile) collapsed to the analytic viewport::camera_lag_px, which derives the same net signed pixel lag as a closed form rather than replicating the accumulator: covered_px = step_progress * METATILE_PX / transit_duration, lag = METATILE_PX - covered_px. A tile is always METATILE_PX (16px) wide regardless of the active crossing's own frame count, so this scales correctly whether the crossing is an ordinary step, a dispatched MB_WALK_* tile (WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE, one pixel per frame) or a dispatched MB_SLIDE_* tile (SLIDE_FRAMES_PER_TILE, two pixels per frame). It is a strictly bigger collapse than SetSpritePosToMapCoords' own entry: that one folds a compile-time constant (the player's own mapX - gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos.x is identically 0), while this folds a per-frame accumulator into a closed form, and only up to the constant term already folded into PLAYER_OBJ_X/Y, so it equals upstream's value on frame-to-frame differences rather than absolutely (see camera_lag_px's docs). Sharing one value keeps the BG scroll in build_tilemaps and the NPC placement in npc::oam_entries in lockstep, so a stationary NPC never snaps to its destination tile at step start while the BG still lags smoothly behind. UpdateObjectEventsForCameraUpdate's own spawn/despawn side effect (TrySpawnObjectEvents/RemoveObjectEventsOutsideView at camera tile boundaries) stays under its own event_object_movement.c ledger entries and is not claimed here.

GetInteractedMetatileScript.script_targe.reason: Classifies all 24 script-returning metatile branches into 23 typed targets, preserving north-facing gates and exact secret-base elevation equality. Furniture and poster save bookkeeping, script launch, services, water-move gating, and cross-kind precedence remain outside this sub-artifact.

GetInteractedObjectEventScript.reason: Selects the visible live object at the front tile, else, only when the front tile is a counter, the one on its far side at the same query elevation (field_control_avatar.c:287-313); an object whose script is null selects nothing and falls through without the counter retry. The result carries the object's local id (gSpecialVar_LastTalked) and the player's facing (gSpecialVar_Facing). Not modelled: writing gSelectedObjectEvent and the special variables, the Trainer Hill script override, and the saved RAM-script override GetRamScript applies.

GetInteractionScript.reason: engine::overworld::select_interaction_target selects the first target of GetInteractedObjectEventScript, GetInteractedBackgroundEventScript, then GetInteractedMetatileScript (script-returning branches only) as a typed InteractionTarget, querying the tile in front of the player at the elevation GetInFrontOfPlayerPosition derives and reading that front tile's metatile behavior (field_control_avatar.c:170-172,240-258). A secret-base entrance already among the caller's saved secret bases selects no background event, so the metatile stage runs next (TrySetCurSecretBase failing, field_control_avatar.c:354-361). Not selected: GetInteractedWaterScript (Surf and Waterfall), because water eligibility depends on party and badge state; launching the selected script, which stays with the caller.

IsArrowWarpMetatileBehavior.reason: engine::overworld::warp::is_arrow_warp_trigger: dispatches by direction to metatile_behavior::is_{north,south,west,east}_arrow_warp exactly as upstream's sArrowWarpMetatileBehaviorChecks table does (field_player_avatar.c:226-232). Issue #174.

RestartWildEncounterImmunitySteps.reason: field_control_avatar.c:662-666. Fully modelled as WildEncounterState::restart_immunity_steps -- zeroes the step counter only, deliberately leaving sPrevMetatileBehavior alone as upstream does (they are two separate statics). Wired at this port's counterparts of upstream's map-load call sites: OverworldPhase::warp_to (LoadMapFromWarp, overworld.c:850) and OverworldPhase::cross_connection (LoadMapFromCameraTransition, overworld.c:800 -- the piece issue #177 explicitly deferred to this slice). The battle-start call sites (battle_setup.c:370, :941) are covered by CheckStandardWildEncounter's own reset on a fired encounter, which upstream also performs (:679).

TryArrowWarp.reason: GetWarpEventAtMapPosition + IsArrowWarpMetatileBehavior + SetupWarp/DoWarp's warp-resolution shape absorbed into engine::overworld::warp::trigger_arrow_warp, a separate entry point from the door-shaped trigger_door_warp precisely because the two are gated differently upstream. Called from crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/step.rs's OverworldPhase::step as a per-frame poll, upstream's own gating: the direction currently held must equal the direction the player currently faces (input->heldDirection && input->dpadDirection == playerDirection, field_control_avatar.c:164-168), evaluated at the tile the player is standing on, independent of tookStep -- so it fires both for a step taken onto an arrow tile while still holding its direction and for a turn in place while already standing on one. The only added gate is that the player be at rest between steps, which is this port's counterpart to the T_TILE_CENTER/T_NOT_MOVING test that sets heldDirection upstream in the first place (:95-112). Issue #174 (the Brendan's-house exit doormat, MAP_LITTLEROOT_TOWN_BRENDANS_HOUSE_1F warp #1 at (8, 8)). Issue #194 corrected the frame ordering against ProcessPlayerFieldInput (overworld.c:1444-1455), which runs this check *before* PlayerStep and skips the step outright when it fires: OverworldPhase::step evaluates this gate ahead of its own movement call and, when it already fires, skips movement for the frame entirely instead of running it and polling afterward -- so a legal, walkable step in the arrow direction warps rather than stepping (previously a permanent no-warp, unreachable on bundled data since every arrow tile's own direction is impassable there, and pinned now by a synthetic scene in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/arrow.rs). Issue #1039 then corrected which frame that single pre-movement poll belongs to. There is now no post-movement poll at all: OverworldPhase::step holds a landing whose walk animation just drained until the *next* call and processes it there, ahead of the arrow poll, because upstream's T_TILE_CENTER needs PlayerCheckIfAnimFinishedOrInactive (field_player_avatar.c:901-915) to see a heldMovementFinished that only the previous frame's CB2 AnimateSprites could have set (main.c:188-195, overworld.c:1438-1469). So a 16-frame tile crossing is polled on call 17, not on call 16: holding the arrow direction through call 16 and releasing it on call 17 does not warp, and the door-shaped trigger_door_warp for that same landing is resolved on call 17 too, above this poll, in ProcessPlayerFieldInput's own order (TryStartStepBasedScript :155-161, CheckStandardWildEncounter :162, then TryArrowWarp :164-168). Pinned by the frame-17 stair-warp regression in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/ordinary.rs and the doormat regressions in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/arrow.rs. Not modelled: StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState's pre-warp avatar snapshot, and SetupWarp's escape-warp/Trainer Hill bookkeeping.

TryDoorWarp.reason: GetInFrontOfPlayerPosition + MetatileBehavior_IsWarpDoor + GetWarpEventAtMapPosition's animated-door gate absorbed into engine::overworld::warp::trigger_animated_door_warp, a new entry point distinct from the completed-step trigger_door_warp. The flow-side decision (facing tile + that gate) is owned by crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/animated_door.rs; OverworldPhase::step only sequences its outcome, pre-movement only (the at-rest preempt, gated on input->heldDirection2 && input->dpadDirection == playerDirection, field_control_avatar.c:175-178, the same held-direction value already computed for the arrow-warp poll). There is no post-movement poll; crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/animated_door.rs owns the timing derivation. The check additionally requires direction == DIR_NORTH (:833-841). Issue #851: a real animated-door tile is always solid, so trigger_door_warp's own completed-step poll (issue #174's TryStartWarpEventScript path) can never reach one -- PlayerState::try_start_resolved_step rejects any nonzero-collision landing before it can exist. Pinned by real Littleroot Town regressions (the Professor Birch's-lab front door, both a stationary approach and a walked one) in flow/overworld_phase/warp_tests/door.rs, by animated_door.rs's own decision tests, and by door_sequencing_tests.rs's drain-call sequencing ratchet (a pack-free whole-frame test cannot observe that one: a failed warp_to preserves map_id and position). Not modelled: TryDoorWarp's secret-base branch, and DoDoorWarp's opening-animation sequence (the warp still resolves immediately, matching every other warp path in this port). Issue #1039 left the pre-movement placement itself untouched but gave it the same frame boundary as every other field-input check: the completed step that the previous call's animation drained is processed at the start of this call, above it, so a coord event, a door-shaped warp or a wild encounter on that landing returns from ProcessPlayerFieldInput (:155-162) before this check at :170-178 runs. A walked approach's door therefore still opens on the call after the approach's animation drains -- upstream's first T_TILE_CENTER CB1 for that crossing -- which is the timing animated_door.rs already derived.

TryStartInteractionScript.reason: OverworldPhase::step's A-press handling routes the target engine::overworld::select_interaction_target selects (object, then background event, then script-backed metatile; GetInteractionScript's order). An object script crate::overworld::npc_scripts::script_text recognizes opens a NpcDialog from that module's own small hardcoded msgbox-style table, and the Route 103 rival object starts its battle. Every other selected target (an unrecognized object script, a sign, hidden item or secret-base entrance, a script-backed metatile) consumes the frame as InteractionOutcome::Unmodelled, matching TryStartInteractionScript returning TRUE for any non-NULL script (field_control_avatar.c:172), but starts no script. A secret-base entrance is selected only when the list of saved secret bases passed to the selector lacks its base, as TrySetCurSecretBase requires (field_control_avatar.c:354-361); the save block holds no secret bases, so this application passes an empty list and every north-facing entrance is selected. Reading the saved bases from the save is not modelled. Only a press that selects nothing lets the frame's direction input reach PlayerState unconsumed. Not modelled: GetInteractedWaterScript, GetInteractedLinkPlayerScript, RamScript, and the interaction sound effect (PlaySE(SE_SELECT)). The lookup runs from the frame-start (pre-movement) player position and facing, before PlayerStep could turn or step the player, matching ProcessPlayerFieldInput reading playerDirection/position before ever calling PlayerStep (field_control_avatar.c:143-145, overworld.c:1444-1455). It sits below the completed step's own events, as upstream does: a landing whose walk animation drained is processed at the start of the next step call (upstream's T_TILE_CENTER CB1, field_player_avatar.c:901-915 over main.c:188-195 / overworld.c:1438-1469), and a coord event, a door-shaped warp or a wild encounter claiming that landing (TryStartStepBasedScript :155-161, CheckStandardWildEncounter :162) returns from ProcessPlayerFieldInput before this check at :172 is ever reached, so the A press is not consumed on that frame.

ShowFieldMessage.reason: Only the held-A/B print speed-up its ExpandStringAndStartDrawFieldMessage(str, TRUE) call enables (field_message_box.c:62-69,118-123 -> AddTextPrinterForMessage(TRUE) -> gTextFlags.canABSpeedUpPrint = TRUE, menu.c:191-...) is modelled: NpcDialog::new unconditionally builds its Printer with Printer::with_ab_speed_up_print, since every caller of that constructor is one of upstream's AddTextPrinterForMessage(TRUE) sites (dialog.rs module docs' 'Held-A/B print speed-up' section, issue #393). NOT modelled in this artifact: sFieldMessageBoxMode's HIDDEN/NORMAL/AUTO_SCROLL state machine (NpcDialog carries no such reentrancy guard), Task_DrawFieldMessage/CreateTask_DrawFieldMessage's two-frame LoadMessageBoxAndBorderGfx-then-DrawDialogueFrame task sequencing, and StringExpandPlaceholders' placeholder substitution (str -> gStringVar4). Issue #1372 additionally threads AddTextPrinterForMessage's TEXT_COLOR_DARK_GRAY/TEXT_COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY (menu.c:191-195) through as FrameAssets::glyph_colors reading the loaded message-box palette's indices 2/3 (text_window.c:93-97), replacing the previous fixed RGB literals the glyph blitter always used regardless of the loaded pack.

ShowFieldMessageFromBuffer.reason: Its StartDrawFieldMessage helper calls AddTextPrinterForMessage(TRUE) unconditionally (field_message_box.c:109-116,125-129) -- always a held-A/B speed-up site, same as ShowFieldMessage's TRUE call -- and modelled the same way: NpcDialog::new's unconditional Printer::with_ab_speed_up_print (dialog.rs module docs' 'Held-A/B print speed-up' section, issue #393). NOT modelled in this artifact: sFieldMessageBoxMode's state machine and the CreateTask_DrawFieldMessage task chain (see src/field_message_box.c#ShowFieldMessage); unlike ShowFieldMessage this function never expands placeholders itself -- it prints whatever the caller already staged in gStringVar4, which this crate has no equivalent global-buffer step for. Issue #1372 additionally threads AddTextPrinterForMessage's TEXT_COLOR_DARK_GRAY/TEXT_COLOR_LIGHT_GRAY (menu.c:191-195) through as FrameAssets::glyph_colors reading the loaded message-box palette's indices 2/3 (text_window.c:93-97), replacing the previous fixed RGB literals the glyph blitter always used regardless of the loaded pack.

CheckForPlayerAvatarCollision.reason: Destination-tile collision check re-implemented via MapRuntime::metatile_cell plus collision.rs's Collision, elevation_mismatch, and directionally_impassable, and (issue #161, I-3 lane) the object-event occupancy test -- the grid collision-bit, directional-impassability, elevation-mismatch and object-event cases, applied in GetCollisionAtCoords' own order (shared between the same-map and connection-crossing step paths via PlayerState::try_start_resolved_step, issue #440). Still not modelled (deferred, all still in v1 scope): the ledge, boulder-push, rotating-gate and acro-bike sub-checks, plus IsCoordOutsideObjectEventMovementRange (never constrains the player) and CanCameraMoveInDirection.

CheckMovementInputNotOnBike.reason: NOT_MOVING/TURN_DIRECTION/MOVING classification re-implemented as PlayerState::step's running-state branch, including the exact turn-vs-step rule (direction change only turns when not already mid-movement)

ForcedMovement_None.reason: Re-implemented inline in PlayerState::step: on a poll off a forced tile, or after a supported forced route is blocked (DoForcedMovement's collision branch, field_player_avatar.c:449-451), movement_direction is reset to facing, releasing a slide's facing lock the way ForcedMovement_None's SetObjectEventDirection(facingDirection) does (:429-440). The facing lock itself is not a stored flag here, because only a dispatch applies it. The PLAYER_AVATAR_FLAG_FORCED_MOVE gate is not modelled, because the reset is a no-op whenever the two directions already agree. enableAnim is covered by the per-crossing TransitCadence.

ForcedMovement_PushedEastByCurrent.reason: The east-ward current pushes the player East through supported_forced_mover on the shared forced-dispatch route at the six-frame current cadence with animation enabled and facing not locked (field_player_avatar.c:521-524).

ForcedMovement_PushedNorthByCurrent.reason: The north-ward current pushes the player North through supported_forced_mover on the shared forced-dispatch route at the six-frame current cadence with animation enabled and facing not locked (field_player_avatar.c:511-514).

ForcedMovement_PushedSouthByCurrent.reason: The south-ward current pushes the player South through supported_forced_mover on the shared forced-dispatch route at the six-frame current cadence with animation enabled and facing not locked (field_player_avatar.c:506-509).

ForcedMovement_PushedWestByCurrent.reason: The west-ward current pushes the player West through supported_forced_mover on the shared forced-dispatch route at the six-frame current cadence with animation enabled and facing not locked (field_player_avatar.c:516-519).

ForcedMovement_Slide.reason: The shared slide helper (sets disableAnim and facingDirectionLocked before DoForcedMovement(direction, PlayerWalkFast), field_player_avatar.c:526-532) for all four MB_SLIDE_* cardinal wrappers: PlayerState's supported_forced_mover maps each standing MB_SLIDE_EAST/WEST/NORTH/SOUTH tile to TransitCadence::SLIDE (SLIDE_FRAMES_PER_TILE, animation_disabled set) with locks_facing set, dispatched by dispatch_forced_mover before the keypad is read. On a successful dispatch movement_direction adopts the forced direction but facing does not, matching SetObjectEventDirection's facingDirectionLocked guard (event_object_movement.c:2361-2370); a blocked route changes neither. animation_disabled is PlayerState::transit_animation_disabled, which crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/overworld/avatar.rs's frame_for reads to hold the go-fast animation's forward-foot cell for the whole crossing instead of switching to the standing pose at the crossing's own halfway point, matching disableAnim pausing the sprite's animator.

ForcedMovement_Slip.reason: Both slip tiles (MB_ICE, the Trick House puzzle floor) dispatch along the player's movementDirection (not facing), crossing at PlayerWalkFast's eight frames with the animation paused and facing not locked, via supported_forced_mover; a blocked route falls through to the keypad (field_player_avatar.c:473-484).

ForcedMovement_WalkEast.reason: DoForcedMovement(DIR_EAST, PlayerWalkNormal): PlayerState's supported_forced_mover maps a standing MB_WALK_EAST tile to (Direction::East, WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE), dispatched by dispatch_forced_mover before the keypad is read.

ForcedMovement_WalkNorth.reason: DoForcedMovement(DIR_NORTH, PlayerWalkNormal): PlayerState's supported_forced_mover maps a standing MB_WALK_NORTH tile to (Direction::North, WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE), dispatched by dispatch_forced_mover before the keypad is read.

ForcedMovement_WalkSouth.reason: DoForcedMovement(DIR_SOUTH, PlayerWalkNormal): PlayerState's supported_forced_mover maps a standing MB_WALK_SOUTH tile to (Direction::South, WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE), dispatched by dispatch_forced_mover before the keypad is read.

ForcedMovement_WalkWest.reason: DoForcedMovement(DIR_WEST, PlayerWalkNormal): PlayerState's supported_forced_mover maps a standing MB_WALK_WEST tile to (Direction::West, WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE), dispatched by dispatch_forced_mover before the keypad is read.

GetPlayerMovementDirection.reason: Movement-direction accessor re-implemented as PlayerState::movement_direction, a field of its own rather than a fold into PlayerState::facing (GetPlayerFacingDirection's target). The forced-movement classification in PlayerState::step reads it for the two behaviors whose handler slips along the player's own direction instead of one fixed by the behavior id (MB_ICE and MB_TRICK_HOUSE_PUZZLE_8_FLOOR through ForcedMovement_Slip/DoForcedMovementInCurrentDirection, field_player_avatar.c:473-484). PlayerState::new, the keypad arms of PlayerState::step, and PlayerState::face set both directions together, as SetObjectEventDirection does (event_object_movement.c:2361-2367). A dispatched slide diverges them: ForcedMovement_Slide sets facingDirectionLocked (field_player_avatar.c:526-532), so the slide's direction reaches movement_direction while facing holds. PlayerState::step resynchronises them on the next poll off the tile or on a blocked forced route, as ForcedMovement_None does (:429-440, :449-451). A START claimed on the landing frame runs before that poll (overworld.c:1444-1455), so OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save writes each nibble of SavedObjectEvent from its own field. MuddySlope's lock and the bike speed it reads stay unported (deferred, still in v1 scope).

PlayerGetElevation.reason: Elevation accessor re-implemented as PlayerState::previous_elevation, the retained previousElevation upstream returns (field_player_avatar.c:1192-1195); PlayerState::elevation is the collision elevation of the current tile

PlayerNotOnBikeMoving.reason: Ordinary-walk attempt-to-move re-implemented as PlayerState::step's Advanced/Blocked branch; a collision starts the interruptible slow in-place bump (see PlayerStep). Surf/run/ledge-jump/boulder-push/rotating-gate/Faraway-Island-Mew special cases and the collision sound are not ported yet -- deferred, still in v1 scope

PlayerNotOnBikeNotMoving.reason: No-input case re-implemented as PlayerState::step's None-input branch (StepOutcome::Idle, running state reset to NotMoving); a neutral poll swallowed by a held collision bump never reaches it, so the movement streak survives until the bump ends or is interrupted

PlayerNotOnBikeTurningInPlace.reason: On-foot standstill direction changes are re-implemented by PlayerState::step as StepOutcome::Turned: facing updates without tile movement, and an eight-frame WALK_IN_PLACE_FAST-equivalent busy timer (TURN_IN_PLACE_FRAMES) now starts, keeping ordinary direction polls Idle through frames 2-8 so a held direction can only begin moving on frame 9 (issue #976). A dialog or the start menu clears that timer immediately on the frame it takes the field lock (PlayerState::clear_turn_lock), matching PlayerFreeze forcing a one-frame face-direction action over an in-flight turn (field_player_avatar.c:1039-1046) so input is live again the frame the overlay closes.

PlayerRideWaterCurrent.reason: Current transit selects the six-frame, non-running, animation-enabled cadence (TransitCadence::CURRENT) used by all four current tiles (field_player_avatar.c:985-988; event_object_movement.c:5828-5889, 8263-8270, 8292-8298).

PlayerRun.reason: A held-B step that clears collision crosses its tile at RUN_FRAMES_PER_TILE (8) frames through PlayerState::step_with_run, plays the running-sheet cells of avatar/run.rs, and drops to walking or standing on the next poll after B is released (field_player_avatar.c:658-668, 995-998). Sound and the bike branch are not ported.

PlayerStep.reason: Per-input-poll orchestration, on-foot only (the bike branch and every special-anim interrupt other than the slow-walk bump below are not ported), re-implemented as PlayerState::step. The WALK_IN_PLACE_FAST turn-in-place case of TryInterruptObjectEventSpecialAnim's non-interruptible window is modeled by the eight-frame turn_frames_remaining busy timer, so ordinary movement input stays gated for the turn's duration unless a dialog or the start menu takes the field lock first, in which case PlayerState::clear_turn_lock ends the window immediately, matching upstream's PlayerFreeze (field_player_avatar.c:1039-1046, event_object_lock.c's Task_FreezePlayer). Forced-movement classification is modeled via is_forced_movement, and the standing tile's dispatch runs before the keypad is read at all, even on a None poll, matching TryDoMetatileBehaviorForcedMovement's placement ahead of MovePlayerAvatarUsingKeypadInput (field_player_avatar.c:332-349): a supported tile commits its direction through resolve_landing/try_start_resolved_step, exactly as DoForcedMovement calls moveFunc on a clear route (:407-470): MB_WALK_* at PlayerWalkNormal's 16 frames per tile (:486-503), MB_SLIDE_* at PlayerWalkFast's 8 with facing locked (:526-552), ice and the Trick House puzzle floor via ForcedMovement_Slip along movementDirection at 8 frames with the animation paused but facing not locked (:473-484), and the four currents via PlayerRideWaterCurrent in their fixed directions at 6 frames with the animation running (:506-524, 985-988; event_object_movement.c:8263-8270). A finished slide crossing keeps its paused forward-foot pose (PlayerState::slide_pose_held) until the next keypad poll, field lock (PlayerFreeze, :1039-1046), or scripted facing, because ForcedMovement_Slide's disableAnim leaves the sprite animation paused until ForcedMovement_None's enableAnim and the standing face-direction action restart it (:429-440, 525-531, 588-600, event_object_movement.c:7302-7313). Every other armed behavior (the waterfall, the muddy slope, and the Secret Base mats, whose ForcedMovement_* physics are not ported) refuses every manual poll, including a would-be turn, except when its own forced direction is itself collision-blocked, in which case (matching TryDoMetatileBehaviorForcedMovement returning FALSE and PlayerStep falling through to MovePlayerAvatarUsingKeypadInput, :342-349) the poll is honoured as an ordinary manual step via the forced_movement_direction/forced_direction_blocked helpers; the Secret Base jump/spin mats never fall through since their handlers never collision-check (:555-565), matching upstream exactly. A supported tile's own blocked forced route leaves the guard armed instead of clearing it: GetForcedMovementByMetatileBehavior re-reads the standing tile's behavior fresh every poll rather than latching a one-time verdict (:409-426), so only a successful dispatch or the player actually leaving the tile clears the guard, and a later poll retries the same dispatch once whatever blocked it (a wall, an object event) no longer does. The keypad still runs on the very poll a blocked attempt was found on (:344-348), and dispatch_forced_mover leaves the movement streak untouched on that blocked attempt, matching DoForcedMovement's collision branch leaving runningState alone (:443-462), so the retry still turns in place first rather than stepping immediately. The guard only arms from a manual MOVING attempt this PlayerState itself made (set in step before collision resolves, from the standing tile's behavior when it has a dispatched handler, so a blocked bump still arms but never traps a deferred behavior, matching upstream selecting MOVING before collision at field_player_avatar.c:583-595; a successful landing then re-arms from the landing tile's own behavior in try_start_resolved_step): a warp arrival or a resumed save that places the avatar onto a forced-movement tile via PlayerState::new starts controllable, since arming on a placement would trap an unsupported behavior with no keypad fallback at all. OverworldPhase::step in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/step.rs suppresses the arrow-warp poll, the animated-door check, the same-frame NPC interaction, and start_menu.rs's OverworldPhase::start_menu_may_open (its sixth gate) on a forced landing's tile-center frame alone, through PlayerState::field_input_suppressed: FieldGetPlayerInput's gate is (T_TILE_CENTER && !forcedMove) || T_NOT_MOVING, so forcedMove, computed from the wider MetatileBehavior_IsForcedMovementTile set rather than the dispatch table, closes only the first arm, and a player at rest on a forced tile still reaches TryArrowWarp/TryStartInteractionScript/TryDoorWarp/pressedStartButton (field_control_avatar.c:93-113). A collision-blocked manual step starts a 32-frame slow in-place walk (BUMP_IN_PLACE_FRAMES, PlayerNotOnBikeCollide's WalkInPlaceSlow, field_player_avatar.c:1011-1015, event_object_movement.c:5713-5735) that PlayerState::step consults before forced dispatch and the keypad, as TryInterruptObjectEventSpecialAnim does (field_player_avatar.c:332-382): a neutral poll or a repeat of the still-blocked direction is swallowed as Idle, and any other poll cancels the bump and is processed normally, so a changed direction steps at once instead of turning. A dialog or menu field lock, a scripted face, or a successful step cancels it too.

PlayerWalkFast.reason: PlayerWalkFast's GetWalkFastMovementAction cadence (sStepTimes[MOVE_SPEED_FAST_1] == 8, event_object_movement.c:8233-8298) is PlayerState::SLIDE_FRAMES_PER_TILE, the crossing duration try_start_resolved_step stores for a dispatched MB_SLIDE_* tile.

PlayerWalkNormal.reason: PlayerWalkNormal's GetWalkNormalMovementAction cadence (sStepTimes[MOVE_SPEED_NORMAL] == 16, event_object_movement.c:8233-8298) is PlayerState::WALK_FRAMES_PER_TILE, the crossing duration try_start_resolved_step stores for both an ordinary step and a dispatched MB_WALK_* tile.

FillConnection.reason: The shared rectangular-copy helper collapses into connected_cell_at's own LayoutGrid::cell_at lookup once its four callers' own coordinate math is inlined per-direction; this port resolves one cell on demand rather than copying a whole strip into a backing buffer, but only within the exact extents that buffer covers (viewport::within_backup_map_band).

FillEastConnection.reason: East-edge offset math (target_x = x - width, target_y = y - offset) re-implemented in connected_cell_at, bounded to gBackupMapLayout's own east cover -- upstream's MAP_OFFSET + 1 copy width (a fixed-buffer sizing artifact of MAP_OFFSET_W's odd total, include/fieldmap.h:19) reproduced as layout-local x <= width + 7 (issue #253).

FillNorthConnection.reason: North-edge offset math (target_x = x - offset, target_y = connected_height + y) re-implemented in connected_cell_at, bounded to gBackupMapLayout's own MAP_OFFSET rows north of the layout (layout-local y >= -7), same shape as FillSouthConnection's own ledger entry.

FillSouthConnection.reason: South-edge offset math (target_x = x - offset, target_y = y - height) re-implemented in connected_cell_at, resolved on demand instead of preloaded, and bounded to the same rows gBackupMapLayout covers -- layout-local y <= height + 6, MAP_OFFSET_H's even total (issue #253).

FillWestConnection.reason: West-edge offset math (target_x = connected_width + x, target_y = y - offset) re-implemented in connected_cell_at, bounded to gBackupMapLayout's own MAP_OFFSET columns west of the layout (layout-local x >= -7); past that the border block renders, exactly as upstream.

GetBorderBlockAt.reason: Border-block fallback for any camera viewport position outside the current layout's own grid, ported into viewport::cell_at over assets::BorderGrid::cell_at, which repeats the shifted 2x2 border and forces MAPGRID_IMPASSABLE collision (rendering-only; movement's own border handling stays out of MapRuntime's scope per issue #108).

GetCameraFocusCoords.reason: The inverse of SetCameraFocusCoords' own entry: reads gSaveBlock1Ptr->pos + MAP_OFFSET back out. Not a separate Rust function -- build_tilemaps derives the player's viewport row directly from PlayerState::position() rather than storing and re-deriving a camera-focus point, but the net player-metatile placement (screen row 72 at rest, issue #977) matches.

GetMetatileAttributesById.reason: Primary-vs-secondary tileset attribute table selection (NUM_METATILES_IN_PRIMARY split) re-implemented in MapRuntime::metatile_behavior

InitBackupMapLayoutConnections.reason: Per-connection dispatch to the four Fill*Connection resolvers re-implemented as connected_cell_at's single match over ConnectionView::direction, called from cell_at on every out-of-bounds viewport sample instead of once per map load into a backing buffer; declaration-order overwrite and the buffer's own coverage band are both preserved (issue #253).

IsCoordInConnectingMap.reason: Single-axis in-range check re-implemented inline in map_runtime::landing_position's bounds test

IsPosInConnectingMap.reason: Perpendicular-axis bounds check for a connection crossing re-implemented in map_runtime::landing_position, called from MapRuntime::resolve_connection

LoadTilesetPalette.reason: combined_world_palette force-writes RGB_BLACK over global color 0 for the primary tileset's bank 0, matching LoadTilesetPalette's forced black write there, and otherwise copies every bank index-for-index from source, matching its unshifted bank copy for the rest of the primary and secondary regions.

CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave.reason: CopyPartyAndObjectsToSave/FromSave (:196-206) and the SavePlayerParty/LoadPlayerParty pair they wrap (:160-178) are OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save (the player object event, then the lead flush) and the lead-owner load OverworldPhase::load_lead_from_save (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/lead_owner.rs), with the flush OverworldPhase::flush_lead_to_save in the same file, called around every start-menu save and on every continue; the party half of both lives in lead_owner.rs, and OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/overworld_phase/start_menu.rs keeps the player object-event write and delegates the party write to the flush. gPlayerParty is this port's single party::LoadedLead (battler, backing record, slot, hidden-HP offset), encoded to and from SaveBlock1::playerParty[party::LoadedLead::slot] -- the continue-selected slot, not a fixed index 0 -- by pokeemerald_rs::party -- species, level, accumulated experience (MON_DATA_EXP, carried since issue #237 made in-battle experience real state rather than a function of the level), personality/nature, the six IVs, the moveset with per-slot PP, the packed ppBonuses byte (issue #304 -- written back byte-exact, including bits for slots the moveset does not fill, so a load/save cycle can no longer strip a save's PP Ups; pinned by pp_ups_survive_the_round_trip_byte_for_byte and pp_bonus_bits_for_unknown_slots_are_not_stripped in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/codec.rs), current HP, the ability slot (issue #322) and the OT id all round-trip, so a continued session fights the mon that was saved. Upstream's copy is a whole-struct assignment; since issue #344 the save half is party::merge_into_save_pokemon, which overlays only those battle-authoritative fields onto the record the slot was loaded from, so everything battle::BattlePokemon does not model -- EVs, held item, contest condition, accumulated friendship, pokerus, met location/level/game, poke ball, OT gender, ribbons, nickname, OT name, language, markings, mail, the egg bit and non-volatile status -- is retained as the save's own bytes rather than rewritten. party::to_save_pokemon writes CreateMon's own default for whichever of those it can derive from its own two arguments (issue #869): nickname (the species' display name), language (GAME_LANGUAGE), met level (the level it was created at, not the level it happens to be when this save runs), met game (VERSION_EMERALD), and poke ball (ITEM_POKE_BALL), same as friendship -- but only where there is no record to retain: a new file's empty slot, or a slot whose personality/OT id says it now holds a different Pokemon. OT name, met location, and OT gender still file zero even there: they need the current save's player identity and map, which to_save_pokemon has no way to see. The cached stat block (max_hp/attack/.../special_defense) is the one group retained *conditionally*: upstream recomputes it at CalculateMonStats call sites and never on load (:170-178 copies bytes and calls nothing), while battle::BattlePokemon rebuilds it from the 0 EVs this port models, so the merge keeps the stored six when species and level are unchanged, and recomputes them via battle::compute_stats_with_evs -- CALC_STAT's own formula, fed the record's retained PokemonSubstruct2 EV bytes rather than the battler's 0-EV BattlePokemon::stats cache -- when the session moved one of those two (an experience change below the level boundary leaves the block retained; pinned by sub_level_experience_does_not_flatten_the_retained_stat_block) -- so loading and re-saving an EV-trained file across a level-up files a block consistent with its own EVs rather than permanently weaker (issue #384; pinned by re_saving_a_loaded_mon_overlays_what_the_session_changed). Current HP is always the battler's, and cannot exceed a retained maximum because the model's own maximum is the 0-EV one; over a retained block the merge adds back the points the load clamp hid (stored hp minus the model's maximum, capped at the retained max_hp, with a fainted battler staying at 0), measured once at load and carried as session state (party::hp_hidden_by_load into the party::LoadedLead's own offset) rather than re-derived from a record the merge itself rewrites, so Continue then SAVE is byte-exact at any stored hp, in-session damage subtracts from the stored value rather than its clamp, and repeated saves file the same bytes (pinned by continue_then_save_keeps_a_full_health_ev_trained_lead_at_full and battle_damage_on_a_clamped_load_subtracts_from_the_stored_hp in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/merge_hp.rs, and saving_twice_in_one_session_files_the_same_bytes in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/save_continue_hp_tests.rs) -- and, since issue #384's round-2 review, that same translation also runs over the freshly *recomputed* block a level-up produces, capped at that maximum instead, with the carried offset first rebased by how much the gap between the EV-aware maximum and the 0-EV floor moved between the old level and the new one (party::zero_ev_max_hp) rather than applied unchanged, so a full-health EV-trained lead that levels up this session still files at full under its new maximum rather than a few points short (pinned by continue_then_save_keeps_a_full_health_ev_trained_lead_at_full_after_levelling_up and a_stat_block_recompute_still_translates_the_load_clamp_offset in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/merge_hp.rs). Pinned by re_saving_an_untouched_lead_writes_the_record_back_byte_for_byte and re_saving_a_loaded_mon_keeps_every_field_the_battle_model_does_not_carry in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/retained_record.rs and by a_re_saved_continued_lead_keeps_the_bytes_no_battle_model_carries in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/save_continue_party_tests.rs. Issue #353 adds a second deliberate divergence, this time on the no-lead arm of the save half: it no longer unconditionally zeroes slot 0. When the load's decode refused slot 0 (recorded in OverworldPhase::undecodable_lead_retained, set by load_lead_from_save's error arm), the save leaves save1.player_party[0] and save1.player_party_count exactly as loaded instead of writing engine::save::Pokemon::default() and a zero count, so a failed secure-region checksum -- or any other party::PartyError, such as an unknown species -- no longer costs the player the whole record (nickname, OT name, language, markings, and the secure bytes themselves) on the very next ordinary SAVE. Upstream needs no such arm because its wholesale gSaveBlock1Ptr->playerParty[i] = gPlayerParty[i] copy achieves the same preservation for free: a Bad Egg (src/pokemon.c:3742-3744 and :4167-4169 set boxMon->isBadEgg = TRUE on a checksum mismatch and leave the mon in gPlayerParty) rides that copy with playerPartyCount unchanged, and LoadPlayerParty validates nothing, so the count rides through the next load too. This port needed the explicit flag only because its decode is a real decode that can refuse where upstream's memcpy cannot -- but as of issue #1371 the save side no longer branches on it either way: a genuinely empty slot (playerPartyCount == 0 at load) takes the exact same untouched-bytes arm as a retained-undecodable one, since ZeroPlayerPartyMons -- which the prior no-lead arm mistakenly cited for the empty case -- is NewGameInitData's and the battle facilities' own reset (new_game.c:143,156,181; battle_factory.c:289,430; battle_tent.c:274; recorded_battle.c:529), never called from the continue/save path. The flag itself survives only as a diagnostic record of why the phase has no lead (OverworldPhase::undecodable_lead_retained's own docs), not as a save-time decision input. Pinned by a_slot_that_will_not_decode_survives_an_ordinary_save, a_deliberate_identity_change_overrides_a_retained_undecodable_slot and a_genuinely_empty_partys_residual_slot_survives_an_ordinary_save in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/save_continue_retention_tests.rs.

SaveObjectEvents.reason: SaveObjectEvents/LoadObjectEvents (:180-194) copy all OBJECT_EVENTS_COUNT entries of gObjectEvents in and out of SaveBlock1::objectEvents. This port models the direction and elevation bytes of one entry: objectEvents[OBJ_EVENT_ID_PLAYER]'s facingDirection/movementDirection nibbles (0xA30 + 0x18), each written from PlayerState's own field, which ShowStartMenu's StopPlayerAvatar (start_menu.c:581-588, field_player_avatar.c:1223-1228, event_object_movement.c:2361-2371) resets to the facing direction before any save (a save opened on a slide's landing frame stores the locked facing in both nibbles), and currentElevation/previousElevation nibbles (0xA30 + 0x0B, include/global.fieldmap.h:232-233) plus the active bit (0xA30 bit 0) and a port marker in the top bit of the third bitfield byte (0xA30+0x03 bit 7, inside the padding:4 upstream leaves unused, include/global.fieldmap.h:227-228), as engine::save::SavedObjectEvent, written by OverworldPhase::copy_party_and_objects_to_save and read back on continue (issue #232: facingDirection and the elevation pair are restored, the loaded movementDirection is ignored and PlayerState starts in step with facing; elevations issue #801: a continue restores the pair verbatim, so history retained on multi-level and transition cells survives, and the saved pair is trusted only when the player object is marked active and its current elevation is one ObjectEventUpdateElevation could hold on the landing cell (the cell's own elevation, or anything on a multi-level cell); the marker is set only by this port's writer, and the writer also stores the object's currentCoords (0xA30+0x10, include/global.fieldmap.h:235) as SaveBlock1::pos plus MAP_OFFSET (7), which a decode requires to match pos, so a pair left behind by a pre-#801 re-save that moved pos while preserving the entry (for example after a downgrade and upgrade) is not trusted either; the save also stamps the save counter its write carries into the entry's initialCoords bytes (0xA30+0x0C, include/global.fieldmap.h:234, unmodeled and untouched by the pre-#801 writer), and SaveStore::load trusts the pair only when the stamp equals the loaded slot's counter, so a pre-#801 save that walks off and back to the same coordinates (every writer advances the counter) is not trusted either; an unmarked image, including an upstream-origin one re-saved by the pre-#801 writer that kept its active bit and a stale elevation byte, falls back to the tile's arrival elevation. A settled player never holds a mismatch on an ordinary cell, since a finished step shifts previous coords to current (ShiftStillObjectEventCoords, event_object_movement.c:2162) before DoGroundEffects_OnFinishStep re-runs ObjectEventUpdateElevation (:8120-8130); the mid-step multi-level early return does not survive to a save). That is the only part of the array a continue observably restores here -- SpawnObjectEventsOnReturnToField respawns the player from it (event_object_movement.c:1715-1726) -- and it removes the DIR_SOUTH stand-in issue #214 recorded. NOT modelled: the other bytes of the player's entry (sprite ids, ground-effect and movement bitfields including facingDirectionLocked, coordinate history, metatile-behaviour history, movementActionId) and every non-player entry, because this workspace models no object-event system to hold them; a save block whose byte is DIR_NONE still falls back to GetAdjustedInitialDirection.

clear_sav.reason: ClearSav1/ClearSav2's zero-the-blocks-when-a-new-game-starts effect is modelled by SaveStore::clear_base, applied on every write of a new-game session (#230 review; #232 review round two). Upstream settles a new game's RAM once -- NewGameInitData memsets gSaveBlock1 via ClearSav1 (new_game.c:160, load_save.c:64-67, which also covers ResetGameStats's gSaveBlock1Ptr->gameStats) and resets gSaveBlock2's deferred state field by field (encryption key :155, ResetPokedex, PlayTimeCounter_Reset), with Sav2_ClearSetDefault -> ClearSav2 on top when the boot load found nothing usable (intro.c:1155-1156) -- and HandleSavingData then writes a whole slot out of that RAM (save.c:736-739) on every save of the session. This port defers unmodelled bytes to the image on disk, so it re-applies the reset per write, and the clear_base input is a property of the *session* (OverworldPhase::new_game_session, read at the store call as game_save::SaveLineage), never of the save mode: keying it off the save type left a new-game session's SAVE_NORMAL retry -- the arm a cleared gDifferentSaveFile produces after a failed overwrite -- writing the replaced trainer's deferred bytes back out. NOT modelled: the RAM struct pointers/shuffling (SetSaveBlocksPointers, MoveSaveBlocks_ResetHeap) and the checksum globals. optionsTextSpeed/optionsWindowFrameType's own boot-verdict carrying is flow::new_game_options_for's contract (issue #1125), not clear_base's; other still-unmodelled SaveBlock2 bytes (e.g. localTimeOffset) remain a real gap, since clear_base drops them with the rest of the deferred payload regardless of boot verdict.

CgbModVol.reason: CgbModVol's envelope-goal/sustain-goal resolution re-implemented as cgb_envelope::cgb_envelope_goal + CgbEnvelope::new/latch_goal, folded in only at note-on and each envelopeCounter==0 boundary via step_with_goal/step_frame; a live track-volume write (CgbVoice::set_track_volume) queues the routing state alone and never latches directly (issue #1210, S-3 slice 2).

CgbOscOff.reason: CgbOscOff's channel-1/2 off-write is reimplemented as SquareChannel::apply_hardware_off_write (crates/audio/src/psg.rs, reached through CgbVoice::apply_hardware_off_write): REG_NR14/REG_NR24 = 0x80 (m4a.c:857-868) clears the frequency register's high three bits, so GBAudioWriteNR14/NR24's catch-up (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:140-194,219-241) rates a later idle-duty advance against the low byte alone rather than the note's last full frequency. The write is also a genuine hardware trigger (GBAudioWriteNR14, mgba/src/gb/audio.c:168-186): it reloads channel 1's sweep from the truncated frequency, rechecks overflow, and revives a muted channel, as SquareChannel::retrigger does. Mixer applies it the instant a Square1/Square2 slot idles, both on TrackStop's immediate clear (src/m4a_1.s#TrackStop) and on natural envelope retirement, tracking the truncated duty position independently of the CgbVoice occupant so the next note-on continues it. NR12=8 leaves the DAC on, so a nonzero-shift channel-1 sweep keeps ticking at 128 Hz and retuning the played frequency while the slot idles (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:965-988); Mixer::mix_frame steps the vacated slot's sweep at the frame's shared tick offsets through CgbVoice::advance_idle_duty, and a sweep overflow mutes the idle channel so its frequency freezes. The idle channel's envelope is dead (volume 0), so GBAudioRun skips its duty catch-up at frame and sweep ticks (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:493-510); the duty catch-up is deferred (SquareChannel::defer_idle_samples) and rated once at the next note-on at the frequency the sweep finally reached. The channel's envelope-silencing half (REG_NR12/REG_NR22/REG_NR42 = 8) remains a byproduct of CgbEnvelope::retire when a note's envelope ends, not a dedicated write; channel 4's noise off-write (NR42 = 8; NR44 = 0x80, m4a.c:873-874) is modeled as a zero-volume preserving retrigger: CgbVoice::apply_hardware_off_write zeroes the hardware volume (HardwareEnvelopeVolume::write_off) and restarts the LFSR and phase (NoiseChannel::retrigger) but leaves the output latch ch4.sample alone, which only an LFSR clock (mgba/src/gb/audio.c:641, lsb * currentVolume) or an envelope step (audio.c:730-732) re-resolves. Mixer applies it on retirement and TrackStop, and the vacated slot keeps its noise clock and phase running and emits the latch through CgbVoice::render_idle_hardware until the first zero-volume clock settles it, so a note triggered inside that period inherits the predecessor's volume-resolved level (NoiseChannel::continue_output_from, 0..=15, never inferred from the predecessor's current volume), rendered against the volume it was resolved at, but only after the replacement's note-on NR43 writes have clocked the held predecessor: NoiseChannel::inherit_hardware_from keeps its whole channel state, and once the initial trigger commits NoiseChannel::commit_initial_writes settles its owed clocks, then installs the replacement's width and clocks the elapsed time at the fastest rate (the width-only write, m4a.c:1020-1022, then the pitched write, m4a.c:1197-1202; mgba/src/gb/audio.c:354-383,602-644) at the predecessor's hardware volume, so the latch left by that catch-up (not the unclocked level) is what the new note holds until its own first clock; the exception is a note that retires on its first envelope pass (zero sustain, no pseudo-echo): m4a.c jumps from the start block to oscillator_off (m4a.c:1040,1090-1102,1125-1129) and never reaches the pitched write, so commit_initial_writes keeps the width-only rate and the off-write restarts channel 4 at that rate rather than the requested pitch; a replacement cancelled before its first pass never consumes the held state; with Mixer::is_idle counting the unsettled idle latch so a fade-end stop does not truncate the tail; channel 3's disable (REG_NR30 = 0) is not modeled.

CgbPan.reason: CgbPan's hard-pan-vs-centre decision re-implemented as cgb_envelope::cgb_pan (S-3 slice 2).

CgbSound.reason: CgbSound's per-hardware-channel envelope, oscillator, and pan loop is re-implemented as cgb_voice::CgbVoice, driven from Mixer::mix_frame. The envelope phase machine, including the pseudoEchoLength pseudo-echo tail (m4a.c:900-1204), is CgbEnvelope. Every CGB_CHANNEL_MO_VOL write CgbSound applies as an NRx4 bit-7 trigger for channels 1, 2, and 4 (m4a.c:1206-1226) -- the envelope phase transitions at m4a.c:1060-1069, 1090-1099, 1125-1137, and 1150-1158, and the live track volume/pan or tremolo LFO write at m4a_1.s:1391-1400 -- re-triggers the oscillator, via CgbEnvelope::step/step_frame/note_off and CgbVoice::set_track_volume reporting the write and CgbVoice::begin_frame applying it through Oscillator::retrigger. A frame that retires the voice applies neither that retrigger nor the NR51 pan commit: its oscillator_off/channel_complete jump (m4a.c:1053-1056, 1084-1101) bypasses the whole CGB_CHANNEL_MO_VOL block (m4a.c:1205-1226), so a volume or pan write pending on the retiring frame never reaches the route the retained hardware keeps; a note's first pass is exempt and keeps its note-on writes. That volume block writes NR14 without NR13 (m4a.c:1219-1225; the pitch block at m4a.c:1198 is NR13's only writer), so channel 1's sweep reloads from the note's high bits rejoined to whatever low byte the sweep has reached, and channel 4's LFSR and clock phase reset. A failing sweep overflow check silences the hardware channel alone: CgbSound holds SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_ON for the note's whole envelope (m4a.c:1055-1058 is its only clearer), so CgbVoice mutes rather than retires and a later safe trigger revives the note. A note whose note-off arrives before its first CgbSound pass takes the SF_START | SF_STOP short-circuit to oscillator_off, retiring at once past the modify/CgbModVol write rather than running the release ramp or the pseudo-echo tail (m4a.c:988-996, 1040-1047, 1053-1057): CgbEnvelope::note_off records the request into the Starting phase and CgbEnvelope::start applies it on that pass, reporting no retrigger. Channel 3 volume follows gCgb3Vol into NR32 (m4a.c:1205-1211): the wave nibble is integer-shifted before centering, so quarter, half, and three-quarter volume quantize neighbouring nibbles together as the hardware does. Channel 3 reloads wave RAM only when the programmable-wave asset identity changes (m4a.c:1003-1012): a note on the same wave, whether it replaces the sounding note or follows retirement, keeps the rotation the prior note left (WaveChannel::continue_rotation_from through Oscillator::carry_hardware_state_from) and restarts only trigger timing, while a different wave loads its table unrotated. A track pitch write is held as a pending request and committed at CgbVoice::begin_frame only when the envelope has not retired: CgbSound's retirement jump to oscillator_off/channel_complete (m4a.c:1053-1056) bypasses the pitch block (m4a.c:1194-1203), so a pitch change on the retiring frame never reaches the retained hardware that the off-write truncates and that later notes continue from.

m4aMPlayFadeOut.reason: m4aMPlayFadeOut/MPlayFadeOut's seeding (m4a.c:58-65, :202) and FadeOutBody's per-frame ramp (m4a.c:692-762, fade-out arm only) reimplemented as MusicPlayer::fade_out and the private FadeOut state: fadeOC/fadeOI/fadeOV with the same 4-per-step drop every 'speed' frames (m4a.c:700, :715) and the same terminal stop-all-tracks state (m4a.c:717-744), stepped once per rendered frame from App::advance_music for the title screen's FadeOutBGM(4) (title_screen.c:784). Each step's volX (m4a.c:756) reaches Sequencer::render_frame_with_fade, which stages it across that frame's ticks and only then re-derives each surviving track's volume through TrkVolPitSet's Rust port (sequencer::track_volume, m4a.c:772), before Mixer::mix_frame sums voices and wraps the DirectSound sum to a signed byte, mod 256 (m4a_1.s:308-339; issue #1243): matching upstream's per-track-then-wrap order instead of the earlier clip-then-scale shortcut that diverged on multi-voice frames that overflow the mix, and matching TrkVolPitSet's single deferred, post-tick propagation (m4a_1.s:1361-1400), which ply_pan and the other volume commands only flag (MPT_FLG_VOLCHG) rather than applying mid-tick -- so neither a track whose Fine lands in that frame nor an intervening PAN receives the step, mirroring ply_fine's flag clear (m4a_1.s:750-777). SoundMainRAM_BoundaryInterpolation.reason: SoundMainRAM's per-output linear interpolation reads the sample one past the current index for its final step before a loop wraps or a one-shot retires (m4a_1.s:399-407), which is the encoded byte wav2agb's payload writer emits past an agbl-trimmed logical count. SoundMainRAM_Exhaustion.reason: SoundMainRAM's shared post-advance exhaustion test, reached by both the TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX path and the pitch-scaled path: the remaining-sample-count subtraction sits after the phase advance inside the per-output DMA loop (m4a_1.s:406-420, subs r2, r2, lr; ble _081DD134) and the non-looping arm stores statusFlags = 0 immediately rather than deferring to the next SoundMainRAM pass (m4a_1.s:376-386, _081DD158.._081DD174). Voice::render re-checks termination immediately after advance_wrapping and retires a non-looping voice in that same render call instead of waiting for a later output slot's pre-render normalize() to catch it, or missing it entirely when the crossing lands in the accumulator's last slot (issue #1078). Still not modelled: SoundMainRAM_ChanLoop's own envelope attack/decay/sustain/release stepping (m4a_1.s ~_081DCF6A-_081DD03A, no separate ledger artifact yet), the PCM DMA ring-buffer's packed four-lane layout via ror 8 (upstream's lanes never carry into each other, since each voice term is masked to a lane's top byte at m4a_1.s:308-339 and :395-416; this crate accumulates each output independently in an i32 and Mixer::mix_frame wraps the finished sum to a signed byte, mod 256, which is the same result), and the raw currentPointer/count pointer bookkeeping beyond the exhaustion test itself.

SoundMainRAM_Reverb.reason: SoundMainRAM's reverb arm (feedback delay line seeding the mix buffer before per-voice mixing) reimplemented as Reverb, wired into Mixer::mix_frame; a song's SongHeader::reverb level enables it via Song::with_reverb/Sequencer::with_config (issue #185). Mixer::mix_frame wraps each DirectSound sample to a signed byte (mod 256, no carry between lanes, matching the masked top-byte lane adds at m4a_1.s:308-339 and :395-416) and commits that DirectSound-only frame to Reverb before CGB voices render, matching SoundMainRAM_Reverb's exclusive DirectSound pcmBuffer feed (m4a_1.s:88-119) and CgbSound's separate NRxx hardware-register path (m4a.c:925-1226); CGB output is mixed in only afterward, for the final output buffer, and never reaches the delay ring (issue #1230).

TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX.reason: SoundMainRAM's fixed-rate DirectSound branch (m4a_1.s:498: tst TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX; movne r8, 0x800000 forces a 1:1 phase step) reimplemented as Voice::fixed_rate forcing the phase step to pitch::FRAC_ONE, which also reproduces the branch's un-interpolated raw-sample reads as a side effect (S-3 slice 3). Covers only this FIX branch, not the rest of SoundMainRAM; the shared post-advance exhaustion test is src/m4a_1.s#SoundMainRAM_Exhaustion. The separate CGB-side use of the flag (m4a.c:1184-1202 8-bit-DAC frequency rounding) is implemented too, recorded on src/m4a.c#TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX (cgb_voice::DacCorrection::apply, PR #276).

TrackStop.reason: Mixer::stop_track reimplements TrackStop's immediate channel teardown: dropping each matching DirectSound or CGB slot absorbs the active-channel status clear (m4a_1.s:1480-1493), the per-channel owner unlink (m4a_1.s:1494-1498), and the track channel-head clear (m4a_1.s:1499-1500). The CGB oscillator-off call itself (src/m4a.c#CgbOscOff) is applied to a vacated Square1/Square2 slot before it drops, truncating the frequency its idle duty catch-up rates against (issue #1482).

ply_endtie.reason: ply_endtie (m4a_1.s:1819-1857) walks a track's channel list picking the first channel matching the played key with SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_START|SF_ENV set and SF_STOP clear, then sets SF_STOP on it alone (issue #901). Reimplemented as Mixer::note_off_track, which instead scans every DirectSound and CGB slot on the track for the requested key and releases the one with the greatest note-on ordinal (mixer.rs note_off_track), a newest-wins equivalent rather than upstream's list-order walk. The CGB side of that eligibility test is now phase-accurate: CgbVoice::is_end_tie_eligible (delegating to CgbEnvelope::is_end_tie_eligible) excludes an automatic pseudo-echo tail and a retired channel, matching ply_endtie's START|ENV/~STOP test, since an automatic zero-sustain tail clears SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_ENV before setting only SF_IEC and never SF_STOP (m4a.c:1090-1098, 1125-1129) and so upstream skips it. DirectSound has no such divergence (m4a_1.s:228-250 keeps SF_ENV set through its own automatic tail) and keeps the plain non-stopping test. Deferred: the list-order-walk mechanism itself and its single-match-then-stop short-circuit are not modeled; note_off_track's newest-ordinal selection is a standing simplification predating this fix.

ply_fine.reason: ply_fine (m4a_1.s:750-777) sets SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_STOP on every still-on channel of the finished track, then unconditionally clears each channel via RealClearChain before resetting the track's flags. It walks track->chan, the single chain ply_note's insertion code (m4a_1.s:1719-1731) shares between SoundChannel and CgbChannel entries (identical track/prev/next offsets, m4a_constants.inc:132-134,251-253), so it also nulls a finished track's CGB channel. Mixer::release_track reimplements the SoundChannel half via Voice::detach_track (issue #1192): select_direct_sound_slot's released-slot tie-break sorts a null owner below every live-owned voice, matching chan->track's null-pointer ordering in ply_note's DirectSound victim loop (m4a_1.s:1694-1711). The CGB half is left attached: not presently player-visible, since add_cgb_voice's reusable test short-circuits on occupant.is_stopping() before ever comparing track (mixer.rs:192-198), and release_track already note-offs a matching CGB voice before returning. Deferred: giving CgbVoice the same nullable ownership, and the doubly-linked chain removal mechanism itself, since Mixer scans its own slot array rather than a linked list.

ply_note.reason: ply_note (m4a_1.s:1538) key-split (TONEDATA_TYPE_SPL) / rhythm (TONEDATA_TYPE_RHY) child resolution, including the pre-allocation no-note path for a nested key-split/rhythm child (m4a_1.s:1604-1609) and, with no upstream equivalent, for an empty child slot (issue #1304), the TONEDATA_TYPE_FIX dispatch bypass, and the pseudoEchoVolume/Length note-on snapshot are reimplemented as sequencer::resolve_instrument + note_on (S-3 slice 3). The channel search is now implemented too (issue #314): sequencer::note_priority sums the song header's priority and the track's PRIO saturated at 0xFF (m4a_1.s:1628-1633) and mixer::Mixer::add_voice/add_cgb_voice reuse a free or released channel, else steal the lowest-priority channel the newcomer outranks (equal priority tie-broken by track order), else refuse the note (m4a_1.s:1647-1718, :1744-1745). Still deferred: ply_note's CGB store path (m4a_1.s:1766-1783) copies ToneData::length into CgbChannel::length (:1771-1772) and normalizes ToneData::pan_sweep into CgbChannel::sweep (:1773-1783; bit 7 set, or no bits of 0x70 set, forces sweep 0x08) -- we model no CGB sound-length counter and pass the voicegroup's sweep byte through unnormalized -- and SoundChannel::count is not seeded from track->unk_3C (:1792-1793).

ply_patt.reason: ply_patt (m4a_1.s:851-869) pushes the return cursor onto track->patternStack and jumps to the target; at the engine's depth of 3 it branches to ply_fine without reading the target. Reimplemented three times: the runtime Track::call_pattern in crates/audio/src/sequencer.rs (three-entry pattern_return_stack, a fourth nested PATT ends the track), the sequence decoder's Event::Pattern/PatternEnd arms in crates/audio/src/sequence/decode.rs (the depth check in crates/audio/src/sequence/reader.rs runs before the operand read), and the extraction decoder in crates/rom-import/src/domains/song.rs, which expands PATT/PEND inline for the pack and terminates a fourth-level PATT as Fine without reading its pointer.

ply_rept.reason: ply_rept (m4a_1.s:880-910) counts repeats per track: a zero count jumps to the target without touching the counter; a positive count increments first, jumps while the counter is below the count, and resets to zero after the final pass, falling through without using the target. Reimplemented twice: the runtime Track::repeat in crates/audio/src/sequencer.rs (lines 216-228, citing m4a_1.s:880-910), and the sequence decoder's Event::Repeat arm in crates/audio/src/sequence/decode.rs (lines 116-131), which keeps the same counter and validates the target only when the repeat is taken.

CB2_WhiteOut.reason: overworld.c:1550-1570. The 120-frame fade-to-black counter, DoMapLoadLoop's map-load state machine, and FieldCB_WarpExitFadeFromBlack's fade-in are not modelled -- this port has no frame-counted fade transition for any warp, matching every other warp/connection crossing's own instant rebind (OverworldPhase::warp_to/warp_to_position/warp_to_saved_location/cross_connection, none of which animate a transition either). Nor is anything else this callback does around the fade: FieldClearVBlankHBlankCallbacks (:1556), StopMapMusic (:1557), and ResetSafariZoneFlag_ (:1558) have no counterparts -- no vblank/hblank callback table is modelled, no map music is playing to stop (crate::music drives the title screen only), and no Safari Zone state exists (though its own persistent flag, FLAG_SYS_SAFARI_MODE, is cleared by DoWhiteOut's own reset -- see src/overworld.c#DoWhiteOut). Of the seven calls upstream makes at the end of the 120 frames, exactly one has a port counterpart that runs: DoWhiteOut (:1559) is OverworldPhase::white_out (see src/overworld.c#DoWhiteOut), called synchronously and immediately, the instant the losing battle's driver reports BattleOutcome::PlayerLost, with no fade in between. The three after it -- ResetInitialPlayerAvatarState (:1560), ScriptContext_Init (:1561), UnlockPlayerFieldControls (:1562) -- run nothing here: this port stores no pre-warp avatar state to reset (see src/overworld.c#GetAdjustedInitialDirection on the missing StoreInitialPlayerAvatarState), has no script engine to re-init, and never locks field controls in the first place (LockPlayerFieldControls is already recorded as unmodelled on src/battle_setup.c#BattleSetup_StartWildBattle), so the map-load-into-overworld handoff white_out performs is just OverworldPhase::warp_to_saved_location's ordinary one (issue #951: the saved-location warp, not the explicit-coordinate warp_to_position).

DoWhiteOut.reason: overworld.c:358-366. Ordering reproduced exactly: SetMoney(&gSaveBlock1Ptr->money, GetMoney(&gSaveBlock1Ptr->money) / 2) is self.save1.money /= 2 (plain unsigned integer division, no rounding); HealPlayerParty() is, since issue #800 (I-6), a full loop over every occupied saved slot: the selected slot heals through battle::BattlePokemon::heal on the phase's one live battler (the party::LoadedLead) when that slot is within the stored count (or the count is still zero, an unsaved new game where slot 0 is the whole live party), and every other occupied slot heals through a decode/heal/merge round trip on its own saved bytes (party::from_save_pokemon/party::merge_into_save_pokemon) -- see src/script_pokemon_util.c#HealPlayerParty. A selected lead beyond a nonzero stored count is not an occupied slot HealPlayerParty's own count-bounded loop would reach, so it merges its current, un-healed battle state back instead (issue #1241). party::select_active_battler is then re-run against all six stored records when the stored count is nonzero (not just the healed, occupied-count-bounded subset -- SetBattlePartyIds's own rescan is over all PARTY_SIZE slots, so a trailing slot beyond the stored count can still hold a real, decodable Pokemon, issue #1241; a clamped stored count of zero skips this rescan entirely and keeps the previously selected lead, the same zero-means-no-lead contract issue #353 established for continue), since an earlier slot the continue-time scan skipped as fainted may now be the first usable one; Overworld_ResetStateAfterWhiteOut's persistent portion (issue #847) is now EventData::clear_white_out_state -- clears FLAG_SYS_CYCLING_ROAD/_CRUISE_MODE/_SAFARI_MODE/_USE_STRENGTH/_USE_FLASH and, when VAR_SHOULD_END_ABNORMAL_WEATHER == 1, zeroes it and VAR_ABNORMAL_WEATHER_LOCATION -- run unconditionally before destination resolution, so a heal location that fails to resolve does not suppress it; SetWarpDestinationToLastHealLocation() + WarpIntoMap() together are self.warp_to_saved_location(map, heal_location) (issue #951: the complete saved WarpData, warp id included, not just map/x/y), map resolved from self.save1.last_heal_location via saved_map_id -- see src/overworld.c#SetWarpDestinationToLastHealLocation and src/overworld.c#WarpIntoMap. NOT modelled: RunScriptImmediately(EventScript_WhiteOut) -- the Elite Four reset and Mr. Briney relocation this port has no state for, and no 'You blacked out!' message box, since this port has no such content bundled and no message layer wired to this path (see data/event_scripts.s#EventScript_WhiteOut); ResetInitialPlayerAvatarState's avatar-transition state this port has no counterpart for. Called from all three battle-loss drivers via the shared OverworldPhase::white_out (module docs' 'RNG stream' section: draws nothing, matching upstream) -- flow::wild_encounter's advance_wild_battle_frame (CB2_EndWildBattle's IsPlayerDefeated branch, src/battle_setup.c:602-616), flow::overworld_phase::route103_rival_trigger's advance_route103_rival_battle_frame (CB2_EndTrainerBattle's, :1333-1338), and flow::overworld_phase::sight_trainer_trigger's advance_sight_trainer_battle_frame (the same CB2_EndTrainerBattle branch, issue #264), each on BattleOutcome::PlayerLost.
