color_effect_blend.reason: effects::alpha_blend/brighten/darken port the hardware BLDALPHA/BLDY per-pixel color-effect math -- the same per-channel weighted-lerp-over-16 formula BlendPalette (util.c) uses for CPU palette fades, generalized to the two-independent-weight (EVA/EVB) form and operating on the compositor's live per-pixel layer stack rather than a static palette buffer, verified against mgba's mColorMix5Bit/_brighten/_darken as compiled for stock desktop mGBA (SDL/Qt) -- the non-COLOR_16_BIT, 8-bit-per-channel path (mgba/include/mgba-util/image.h:15-20, 253-266, 307-327; mgba/src/gba/renderers/software-private.h:237-245, 270-278), since COLOR_16_BIT is only ever defined for the Wii/3DS/libretro build targets (mgba/src/platform/wii/CMakeLists.txt:11, mgba/src/platform/3ds/CMakeLists.txt:14, mgba/CMakeLists.txt:1026), never desktop, and docs/acceptance/v1.md's binding gate is the observable experience on mGBA (docs/principles.md's reference-only). Those three routines mask each channel in place in the packed u32, so _darken's shifted (green/blue) lanes subtract ceil(c*y/16) where its low (red) lane subtracts floor(c*y/16) -- _darken(0xFFFFFF, 7) is (144, 143, 143) -- and darken_red_channel/darken_shifted_channel reproduce both, pinned by an exhaustive oracle test over every 5-bit channel value and every usable EVY (S-2 slice 4, issue #99; corrected to the 32-bit oracle in issue #380). The rest of palette.c (BeginNormalPaletteFade/UpdatePaletteFade's CPU fade sequencing, TintPalette_GrayScale/_SepiaTone, InvertPlttBuffer) remains pending -- distinct software palette-buffer features, not this hardware register path. OBJWIN-masked forced-alpha composition selects a target-1 BG's brighten/darken variant (effects::objwin_bg_variant) when the OBJWIN region enables effects, before mixing it as the immediate target 2, while unmasked forced-alpha BG neighbors stay normal (mgba/src/gba/renderers/software-private.h:87-125,156-171); pinned for regular and affine BGs by crates/rendering/src/compositor/tests/objwin.rs (issue #1794).

CalculatePPWithBonus.reason: pokemon.c:4650-:4654, plus the gPPUpGetMask/gPPUpClearMask tables it reads (:1857-:1866). Fully modelled (issue #304) as battle::pokemon::pp_bonuses: PpBonuses is upstream's packed ppBonuses byte (two bits per move slot, struct PokemonSubstruct0::ppBonuses at include/pokemon.h:104 and struct BattlePokemon::ppBonuses at :288) as an owned type, and calculate_pp_with_bonus is basePP + ((basePP * 20 * ppUps) / 100) with upstream's single trailing truncation rather than a per-Up one. BattlePokemon carries the byte whole (not a per-slot field) so the save round trip is byte-exact, including bits belonging to a slot the moveset does not fill; PpBonuses::get is the (gPPUpGetMask[i] & bonuses) >> (2 * i) read and PpBonuses::cleared is gPPUpClearMask's write. Every one of the 256 bytes is accepted -- two-bit fields cannot overflow, so there is nothing to reject. BattlePokemon::max_pp is the per-slot application: it is what HealPlayerParty restores to and what deduct_pp counts down from. The arithmetic runs in u32 and saturates back to u8 where C would wrap, unreachable for real data (the largest gBattleMoves pp is 40, giving 64 fully upgraded). NOT modelled: applying a PP Up at all -- ITEM4_PP_UP's gPPUpAddValues path (:4958-:4972) and the Max Elixir-style :5256-:5264 case need an item-use path this port does not have, so a nonzero byte can only arrive from a save file today.

MonTryLearningNewMove.reason: pokemon.c's level-up move learning (MonTryLearningNewMove, :3014-:3044, and GiveMoveToMon/GiveMoveToBoxMon, :2934-:2955), reached in-battle from Cmd_getexp via BattleScript_LevelUp -> Cmd_handlelearnnewmove (battle_script_commands.c:5360) and in the overworld from the daycare/evolution paths (still not modelled -- see below). As of issue #252, BattlePokemon::apply_experience (walk in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs) spends the award one level threshold at a time in ascending order, upstream's own consumption shape (Task_GiveExpToMon's cap at nextLvlExp, battle_controller_player.c:1154-:1181, looped by Cmd_getexp case 5), and offers each of that level's assets::LevelUpLearnsets entries, in table order, to GiveMoveToBoxMon's two outcomes: a move already known is skipped at no slot cost (MON_ALREADY_KNOWS_MOVE, :2951-:2952), and a move with an empty slot is learned into it at its own base PP (:2945-:2949, writes at :2947-:2948). Teaching is UNSCREENED, exactly as upstream teaches: whatever move id the learnset names is learned, including one whose effect this crate has no resolver for -- a level-6 Treecko learns Absorb even though EFFECT_ABSORB is unmodelled (crate::hit's module docs). That needs no screen because this path only runs on the PLAYER's mon, and the player's moveset is the one Battle::new documents as deliberately unscreened (only the wild mon is screened at Battle::new, whose rejection loop can land on any slot mid-turn; new_trainer separately screens the trainer's whole party for its own documented bench-arrival reason); a player slot is validated per turn at selection by validate_player_move, ahead of the turn's first RNG draw, and an unexecutable pick is refused with a recoverable BattleError that leaves the battle usable. The four-known-moves case is no longer a divergence: as of issue #304 it is modelled as the pause upstream makes. MON_HAS_MAX_MOVES (:2954) stops the walk and parks a PendingMoveLearn ON THE MON (BattlePokemon::pending_move_learn) -- gMoveToLearn plus the resume position upstream keeps in the sLearningMoveTableID file-static (:3021), owned state exactly as upstream's globals are, so a stale copy cannot be replayed and one mon's prompt cannot be answered on another -- which is upstream reaching BattleScript_AskToLearnMove's yes/no box (battle_script_commands.c:5368-:5370); the pause holds the mon AT the prompted level, the award's remainder unconsumed on the token, so a prompt never exposes prematurely raised levels or stats. Nothing is learned until BattlePokemon::resolve_move_learn is given a MoveLearnDecision, and apply_experience's return is #[must_use] so a caller cannot overlook the open question. Declining resumes the same walk at the next entry exactly as BattleScript_TryLearnMoveLoop does; replacing a slot performs both of Cmd_yesnoboxlearnmove's writes in upstream's order, RemoveMonPPBonus then SetMonMoveSlot (:5479-:5480), so the forgotten move's PP Ups go with it and the incoming move starts at its own base PP. The walk lives in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs; crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/move_learn.rs is where this port's three headless drivers answer, with the documented stand-in (decline) they use for every other absent player input, since there is no battle scene to ask in. NOT modelled from the replacement path: the yes/no box, the summary-screen move list (ShowSelectMovePokemonSummaryScreen, :5449), and every string. IsHMMove2's refusal to overwrite an HM slot (:5468-:5472) IS modelled -- BattleError::HmMoveCantBeForgotten, refused before any write with the prompt left answerable, because a loaded save (or the unrestricted constructor) can legitimately hold an HM move even though no learnset names one; see src/battle_script_commands.c#Cmd_yesnoboxlearnmove. Pinned in crates/battle/src/pokemon/learn.rs's own tests (pause, decline, replace-clears-the-bonus, resume), crates/battle/tests/turn_engine/trainer_battle.rs (a_full_moveset_asks_before_learning_and_honours_either_answer, a_trainer_battles_exp_award_surfaces_the_replacement_prompt, a_multi_level_jump_learns_each_crossed_levels_moves_in_order) and crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/flow/move_learn/tests.rs (a driver that leaves the prompt unanswered abandons a winnable fight). The overworld Move Reminder/Deleter and evolution move learning remain out of scope. The save decoder deliberately never reaches this walk: from_save_pokemon reconciles a stored experience total through BattlePokemon::reconcile_saved_experience (level derivation only, the GetLevelFromMonExp-on-load shape -- upstream copies the attacks substructure verbatim and never teaches on load), pinned by decoding_an_inconsistent_save_levels_up_without_teaching_moves in crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/codec.rs.

HealPlayerParty.reason: script_pokemon_util.c:30-59. battle::BattlePokemon::heal reproduces the per-mon effect for the one party slot this crate models (the crate's own module docs record the one-mon-party limit): restore current HP to Stats::max_hp (upstream's MAX_HP write, :39-42), restore every known move's PP to BattlePokemon::max_pp, which is upstream's own CalculatePPWithBonus(move, ppBonuses, j) (:47) -- as of issue #304 the ppBonuses byte is real state (see src/pokemon.c#CalculatePPWithBonus), so a slot carrying PP Ups heals to the UPGRADED maximum rather than to the move's base PP; pinned by heal_restores_pp_to_the_pp_up_adjusted_maximum (crates/battle/src/pokemon/tests.rs) and healing_a_restored_mon_refills_to_the_upgraded_maximum (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party/tests/codec.rs). Upstream's third effect -- zeroing MON_DATA_STATUS (:52-57) -- now has a partial in-model counterpart since issue #783: battle::status1::Status1 models paralysis, and heal() clears it to Status1::Healthy in the same pass as HP and PP (pinned by heal_cures_primary_status, crates/battle/src/pokemon/tests.rs). That clear is in-battle-only, though: the party-level status BYTE this file's own module docs describe is a separate, still-unmodelled thing (crates/pokeemerald-rs/src/party.rs's module docs) -- party::merge_into_save_pokemon retains it from the backing record untouched across an ordinary save, so heal()'s in-memory Status1 clear and the retained save-format byte can disagree until a later slice wires Status1 into the merge like any other battle-owned field, matching this crate's parallel EV precedent. The white-out call site still separately clears the retained record's status byte, now through the lead owner's flow::overworld_phase::lead_owner::OverworldPhase::heal_whole_lead rather than by editing the lead fields in flow::overworld_phase::white_out (pinned by white_out_clears_stored_status_before_an_immediate_save), which is the other half of this same still-open split. The loop over gPlayerPartyCount (:37) is the call site's own responsibility, not this method's: since issue #800 (I-6), both flow::overworld_phase::white_out::OverworldPhase::white_out and flow::overworld_phase::first_battle_conclusion::OverworldPhase::conclude_first_battle share one call-site routine, flow::overworld_phase::white_out::OverworldPhase::heal_whole_party_and_reselect_lead, that loops every occupied slot itself, healing the selected slot through this method's live battler when that slot is within the stored count (or the count is still zero, an unsaved new game) and every other occupied slot through a decode/heal/merge round trip on its own saved bytes (party::from_save_pokemon/party::merge_into_save_pokemon) -- a selected slot beyond a nonzero stored count merges its current, un-healed battle state instead (issue #1241) -- then re-runs SetBattlePartyIds's own active-battler re-scan, over all PARTY_SIZE slots for a nonzero stored count (party::select_active_battler) -- a clamped stored count of zero skips this rescan by the same zero-means-no-lead design issue #353 established -- see src/overworld.c#DoWhiteOut for the widened call site's own citation. Three flow-level callers share this one primitive (oop-boundaries): flow::overworld_phase::white_out::OverworldPhase::white_out (issue #261, DoWhiteOut's own HealPlayerParty call on a wild/trainer loss, alongside a money halve and a heal-location warp neither belongs to this method); since issue #251, flow::overworld_phase::first_battle_conclusion::OverworldPhase::conclude_first_battle (Route101_EventScript_BirchsBag's own special HealPlayerParty, with no accompanying money halve or heal-location warp -- the only respects in which it is narrower than white_out's call, not in slot coverage: both now heal and reselect across the whole party, per issue #800); and flow::overworld_phase::OverworldPhase::from_saved's legacy-save migration (PR #291 review), a port-only call with no upstream counterpart -- upstream's load path never heals -- that repairs the fainted lead only a pre-#251 build could have serialized after a lost first battle.

UpdateOamCoords.reason: The coordOffsetEnabled branch (gSpriteCoordOffsetX/Y added to an enabled sprite's OAM position) ported as npc::oam_entries' own camera_lag addition inside object_screen_position (issue #217, I-3) -- the fix for NPC sprites snapping to their destination tile at step start instead of staying glued to the camera through the walk animation. The branch *selection* (which sprites opt in) is not modelled, and honestly cannot be split by sprite: upstream sets coordOffsetEnabled = TRUE unconditionally in TrySetupObjectEventSprite (src/event_object_movement.c:1466), which every object event reaches -- the player's own included (InitPlayerAvatar -> SpawnSpecialObjectEvent -> TrySpawnObjectEventTemplate -> TrySetupObjectEventSprite; src/field_player_avatar.c:1399, src/event_object_movement.c:1490,1507). So the offset is on for every sprite this module draws and the branch is unconditional here. The player nevertheless looks screen-fixed upstream (and is drawn at the fixed avatar::PLAYER_OBJ_X/Y here) for a different reason than 'no offset': its own walk animation advances sprite->x/y by 1px/frame along travel (Step1, src/event_object_movement.c:8191), cancelling the coord offset frame for frame. This port collapses that cancellation to a constant rather than reproducing both halves -- see SetSpritePosToMapCoords' own ledger entry.

affine_oam.reason: sprite_affine::sample_texel (paired with OamEntry::AffineMode/with_affine/bounding_box in oam.rs) ports affine and affine-double-size OBJ sampling: matrix-group selection by matrixNum (0..=31, gOamMatrices), the double-size bounding box (CalcCenterToCornerVec's ST_OAM_AFFINE_DOUBLE doubling), and center-relative texture-space sampling biased onto the nominal (undoubled) texture, verified pixel-for-pixel against mgba's GBAObjAttributesAIsTransformed branch and xAccum/yAccum setup (software-obj.c:215-316) including the outside-texture-vs-transparent-hole distinction that feeds SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel's priority-upgrade rule. h/v flip are correctly ignored once affine (hardware reuses those bits as matrixNum bits 3-4). The rotation/scale-to-matrix computation (ObjAffineSet/SetOamMatrix trig side) is not modelled -- only matrix selection and consumption are. sample_texel's local_x parameter also carries SpriteLayer::sample_affine_local's OBJ-mosaic caller (S-2 issue #802, complements oam_mosaic): a mosaic-enabled affine entry passes a signed footprint-local column that can be -1 (a leading block held one column before the sprite's own edge, mirroring mgba's SPRITE_TRANSFORMED_MOSAIC_LOOP pre-loop seed at source position inX-1, software-obj.c:53,241) or a column past the bounding box (a mosaic-extended trailing block); both resolve through the existing post-transform out-of-source check rather than a separate pre-transform bound. An ObjMode::Window affine entry still reaches this mosaic path but with MosaicSize::vertical_only (crate::mosaic): SpriteLayer::sample_entry_mosaic keeps the vertical row snap mgba applies unconditionally before dispatch (video-software.c:1027,1042-1050) while never holding the transformed position across a horizontal block, matching mgba's unconditional non-mosaic SPRITE_TRANSFORMED_LOOP for FLAG_OBJWIN (software-obj.c:287-288/303-304). Windows/blending otherwise remain out of scope (issue #98).

oam_admission.reason: Not a port of any pokeemerald src/sprite.c function -- pokeemerald itself assumes unlimited per-scanline OAM processing and never models the GBA's fixed OBJ cycle budget. Filed here (alongside affine_oam/oam_mosaic) as the sprite renderer's third mgba-verified hardware-timing artifact: OamAdmission::for_scanline (crate::oam_budget) ports the GBA PPU's real per-scanline OAM admission -- a fixed cycle budget (mgba/include/mgba/internal/gba/video.h:36-37: OBJ_LENGTH=1210 normally, OBJ_HBLANK_FREE_LENGTH=954 when DISPCNT's HBlank-interval-free bit is set, mgba/src/gba/renderers/video-software.c:623) that caps OAM traversal at 128 physical entries (mgba/src/gba/renderers/common.c:13) and drops late sprites/OBJWIN masks once exhausted. sprite_list_cost ports mgba's OAM clean pass (common.c:18-45): an entry that is disabled (common.c:18) or lies entirely off the left edge, x + width < 0 (common.c:34-36 for a regular entry; common.c:43-45, which tests the raw 9-bit X field, rejects an affine one on the same condition), never enters the sprite list at all -- it is neither drawn nor charged its own cost, only the traversal its index contributes. Costs are mgba's two unclipped formulas (common.c:24-39), taken over the entry's bounding-box width (already doubled for AffineDoubleSize per common.c:26): affine 8 + width * 2 then += x when x < 0; regular width - 2 then += x >> 1 when x < 0 (C's arithmetic shift, which Rust's i32 >> reproduces). mgba never clips width to the on-screen part, and the two kinds fall off at different rates: a 64-wide entry costs 62 (regular) / 136 (affine) at x=0, 46 / 104 at x=-32, 30 / 72 at x=-64. The walk itself is video-software.c:1029-1064's charge-then-check ordering: traversal is 2 * (index - lastIndex) with lastIndex starting at 0, so OAM index 0's traversal is free and every later slot costs 2; the charge lands before the exhaustion test; that test is remaining <= 0, not < 0; an off-scanline entry is skipped only after both (video-software.c:1040-1042); and an admitted entry's own cost is deducted only after processing (video-software.c:1064), so a sprite whose own cost crosses zero is still drawn and only the next slot's traversal stops the rest. common.c:43-45's rejection of entries entirely off the *right* edge (x >= 240 -- the raw 9-bit X band 240..=255, which decodes to no visible pixel) is modelled the same way: such a slot retains only the walk's traversal cost and cannot drain the per-scanline budget or displace a later visible sprite (oam_budget.rs's right-edge tests); the case is reachable, snow weather parks wrapped flakes near x = 242 (src/field_weather_effect.c:970). SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel and SpriteLayer::objwin_mask (sprite.rs) both gate their entry iteration through this single admission stage -- reading it out of one per-scanline cache slot (SpriteLayer::with_admission), which both keeps the walk to once per scanline rather than once per pixel per path and makes it structurally impossible for visible resolution and OBJWIN masking to disagree about which entries a scanline exhausted. SpriteLayer::with_hblank_free_interval threads DISPCNT's HBlank-interval-free bit in from the caller -- pokeemerald sets that bit unconditionally in the overworld's DISPCNT setup (src/overworld.c:2122-2123; that file is still ledger-pending overall and this bit is not yet its own tracked artifact), so a future caller wiring live DISPCNT state through gets the reduced 954-cycle budget for free. Issue #329 (S-2).

oam_mosaic.reason: OamEntry::mosaic/with_mosaic port OamData's OBJ mosaic bit. SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel_with_mosaic/objwin_mask_with_mosaic snap a mosaic-enabled Regular entry's sampling coordinate to its MOSAIC-register OBJ block origin (crate::mosaic) before sampling, verified against mgba's SPRITE_MOSAIC_LOOP macro (S-2 slice 4, issue #99). A mosaic-enabled affine entry instead holds the *transformed* source position across a screen-space block (SpriteLayer::sample_affine_local, S-2 issue #802), verified against mgba's distinct SPRITE_TRANSFORMED_MOSAIC_LOOP macro (software-obj.c:49-71, selected at :289-295/:305-311): it rejects an out-of-source position after transforming rather than clamping the bounding-box coordinate before transforming, so a leading partial block can sample outside the nominal texture and stay unwritten, unlike the regular loop's edge clamp. Vertical mosaic snapping stays shared between both dispatch branches (mgba clamps the source scanline identically before either loop runs, video-software.c:1027-1050). SpriteLayer::sample_entry_mosaic keeps only that vertical snap for any ObjMode::Window entry (both Regular and affine) via MosaicSize::vertical_only, matching mgba snapping the source row before dispatch regardless of FLAG_OBJWIN (video-software.c:1027,1042-1050) while selecting the unconditional non-mosaic (non-block-holding) loop horizontally whenever FLAG_OBJWIN is set -- the mosaic-rounded trailing draw condition still applies too, since mgba computes it unconditionally before that dispatch (software-obj.c:233-239 affine, :320-325 regular; loop selection at :344-345/360-361 regular, :287-288/303-304 affine). Complements oam_regular_fields/affine_oam/oam_obj_mode. An affine hold additionally restarts at each hardware-window span's own start rather than only at a mosaic block boundary, porting mgba's per-span sprite preprocessing rerun (software-obj.c:227-242, video-software.c:1052-1062): compose_frame_with_effects (crates/rendering/src/compositor.rs) threads each scanline's window span starts and per-span OBJ-pass eligibility into SpriteLayer::resolve_pixel_with_mosaic_windowed's WindowSpans, whose sample_affine_local seeds a held sample from inX-1 at its own span's start instead of the mosaic block's, and searches later OBJ-drawing spans for a trailing spill the sprite's own raw edge binds past its span, sharing the same same-entry write lock that stops a contested slot's spill search at its first candidate span (software-obj.c:79-85). Separately, an OBJWIN entry's contribution -- opaque or a transparent hole -- is dropped per the *writing* span whose own rank outranks OBJWIN's, not the queried column's (software-obj.c:161, video-software.c:131-134): SpriteLayer::sample_entry_mosaic and sample_affine_local filter candidate spans on WindowSpans::suppresses_objwin/span_suppresses_objwin so a WINOUT pass's OBJWIN hole still promotes a worse-priority OBJ under its trailing spill even where that spill lands inside WIN0/WIN1, which a queried-column-only suppression check would wrongly discard (S-2, issue #1084). objwin_mask_with_mosaic never receives this span state and always samples with WindowSpans::WHOLE_SCANLINE, because OBJWIN is a per-pixel mask rather than a hardware-window span and mgba never restarts a hold for it (S-2, issue #1084). The draw-time brighten/darken variant and FLAG_REBLEND postpass a written OBJ pixel carries are SpritePixel and effects::resolve_pixel_color's concern (S-2, issue #1305), independent of which span the mosaic hold or OBJWIN suppression above resolves.

oam_obj_mode.reason: OamEntry::mode/with_mode/ObjMode port OamData's objMode field (attr0 bits 10-11): SemiTransparent forces the sprite's pixel to alpha-blend against a valid second target behind it, unconditionally overriding whichever color effect BLDCNT actually selected, and Window contributes only to the OBJWIN mask (SpriteLayer::objwin_mask) rather than drawing a pixel of its own -- both verified against mgba's software-obj.c (S-2 slice 4, issue #99). Complements oam_regular_fields/affine_oam, which cover the rest of OamData's fields.

oam_regular_fields.reason: OamEntry/ObjShape/obj_dimensions port the regular (non-affine) OBJ attribute fields sprite.c populates: screen position (with the 9-bit sign-extended X and modulo-256-wrapping Y verified against mgba's software-obj.c), tile index, 4bpp palette bank/8bpp flag, H/V flip, the twelve square/wide/tall shape-size pairs, priority, and enabled state; affine attributes are out of scope (issue #64).

RenderText.reason: The per-frame RENDER_STATE_HANDLE_CHAR loop -- newline, \l/\p prompt-scroll/prompt-clear wait-then-act states, glyph-id resolution via the decoded byte, and the reveal-delay countdown -- reimplemented as Printer::tick's frame-driven state machine (PrinterState). Faithful to upstream's unconditional 'delayCounter = textSpeed' reload before each consumed char: a RENDER_REPEAT-class token (newline, no-op control code, skipped placeholder) reloads the reveal-delay counter and re-enters HANDLE_CHAR, so at Slow/Mid (textSpeed != 0) it costs one full reveal-delay period rather than being frame-free, and the first glyph after a \l scroll or \p page clear resumes with delayCounter = textSpeed; at Fast/Instant (textSpeed == 0) those tokens stay free. Colour/font/audio extended control codes are consumed as documented no-ops; see the module's 'Deliberately out of scope' docs. EXT_CTRL_CODE_PAUSE is no longer among them (issue #393): it is a modelled render state -- PrinterState::Pause mirrors upstream's RENDER_STATE_PAUSE (text.c:1215-1220), counting the control code's argument frames down before returning to HandleChar. EXT_CTRL_CODE_CLEAR and EXT_CTRL_CODE_CLEAR_TO have left that no-op set too (issue #1273): both keep upstream's width > 0 guard (text.c:1063-1090) -- CLEAR erases its argument's width at the cursor and advances past it, CLEAR_TO erases forward to the origin-relative column and so never moves the cursor back, unlike its sibling SKIP -- and a clear that did erase ends the frame the way upstream's RENDER_PRINT does, while a clear with nothing ahead stays a free RENDER_REPEAT. The erased rectangle is reported through Printer::cleared_span rather than painted; see src/text.c#ClearTextSpan. EXT_CTRL_CODE_FILL_WINDOW has left that no-op set too (issue #1368): it fills the whole window with the background colour and resets both cursor axes to the printer origin before continuing within the same frame as RENDER_REPEAT (text.c:1048-1057), surfaced through Printer::cleared_window rather than painted, same as the CLEAR/CLEAR_TO span above.
